newsitem.title: BRAZIL: PACTUAL-LED FIRM BUYS CREDIREAL FOR 121 MLN REAIS.
newsitem.headline: PACTUAL-LED FIRM BUYS CREDIREAL FOR 121 MLN REAIS.

text.p: A company led by Brazil's Banco Pactual bought a controlling stake in Minas Gerais state bank Credireal for the base price of 121.3 million reais at a closed-envelope auction on Thursday, the bolsa said.
Companhia de Investimentos Latinoamericana was the only investor that placed a bid at the auction, the Minas Gerais-Espirito Santo-Brasilia Stock Exchange (BOVMESB) said.
The other two bidders -- Varejo S.A. Administracao e Participacao, a unit of local Bozano, Simonsen group and Banco Industrial e Comercial (Bicbanco) -- declined to present price offers.
Cia de Investimentos Latinoamericana was created by local Banco Pactual to seek opportunities in Brazil's banking sector for domestic and foreign investors.
It was not immediately clear which investor the company represented.

Minas Gerais state government sold a total of 986.672 million shares, representing 89.9 percent of Credireal's total capital, at the auction as a 10 percent stake reserved to staff was fully acquired by the bank's employees, retirees and pension fund.

Credireal, formally known as Banco de Credito Real de Minas Gerais SA, was the second Brazilian state-owned bank to be privatized. The first was Rio de Janeiro state bank Banco Banerj SA, which was bought by Brazil's Banco Itau.
